set.v: $240 in gold (twelve double eagles) and two silver half dollars in an iron pot (recovered)
set.st: In August 1900 Capt. Zach G. Suiter of Le Claire, digging for fish worms in a cellar, found a pot of gold and silver coins, silver dated to 1818 and gold to 1850, in a house built in 1850 that had once been a saloon. The papers joked that it was Buffalo Bill's first savings, since Cody grew up in Le Claire. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. The Marshalltown paper adds that he was a river man formerly of the steamer Verne Swain, that the iron pot held $200-300 in gold and two silver pieces, and that the house had been a saloon when Le Claire 'was one of the toughest river towns along the Mississippi'; it supposed someone in trouble buried the pot and never came back. The Davenport paper, next day, counts the pot at twelve double eagles and two half dollars, and says no one else claimed it.
src: Davenport Daily Leader, 30 Aug 1900, p. 7 (local report, next day; Newspapers.com 36945810)
